critical_issues.msg: Token fallback to GITHUB_TOKEN defeats the PAT purpose — events from GITHUB_TOKEN do NOT fire pull_request workflows, so downstream CI will not trigger after the auto-commit.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove `|| secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` and guard with a required secret or a condition: only run the commit step when `secrets.COMMIT_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set. Alternatively, document why the fallback is intentional and accept the missing downstream CI trigger.

suggestions.msg: actions/setup-node@v4 installs Node.js but fix_pr_comments.py is a Python script with no Node dependency.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the `actions/setup-node@v4` step and the `Set up claude` step (lines 65-73) — neither is used by the Python script.

suggestions.msg: Refresh step (lines 80-95) and exclude cycle (lines 162-174) add complexity: files are fetched from master only to be immediately dropped from the commit. The same logic is duplicated across two separate code paths.
suggestions.suggestion: Simplify by never staging those two files in the first place: `git add -A -- :!scripts/ci/fix_pr_comments.py :!scripts/ci/fetch_pr_test_failures.py`, or use a .gitattributes exclude rule.

suggestions.msg: run_gh has no timeout — if `gh` hangs (network issue, credential prompt), stream_claude will block indefinitely even though the outer caller has a timeout budget.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a reasonable timeout to the subprocess.run call in run_gh, e.g. `timeout=30`, and handle subprocess.TimeoutExpired by logging and returning an error result.

suggestions.msg: url.removeprefix/.removesuffix are Python 3.9+; the workflow specifies Python 3.11 so this is fine, but the shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env python3`) may resolve to Python 3.8 on some systems.
suggestions.suggestion: Pin the shebang to python3.11 or use `/usr/bin/env python3` as a portable fallback and rely on the workflow to set the correct Python.

suggestions.msg: pr_number argument is extracted from env and cast to int; if the env var is an empty string the early return on line 335 catches it, but a 0-valued PR number would not be caught (int('') raises, but '0' is valid and would pass).
suggestions.suggestion: Add `if pr_n <= 0: log(f'invalid_PR_NUMBER={pr_n}'); return 1` after the int cast on line 346.
